title: Answer a tax-authority notice
summary: Most tax notices are not audits. They point at one mismatch and print a response deadline on the first page (in the US, law rule us-fed.cp2000-response-deadline: the CP2000 reply is due by the date listed on the notice). Read the notice code, pull that period's records, and recompute the number they claim is wrong. Then respond by the deadline: agree and pay, or contest with documentation. If the response needs a signed statement, the signature is yours, sometimes under penalty of perjury. Educational guidance, not legal advice. The deadline that matters is printed on your notice; verify it there.

geoNotes.summary: A Steuerbescheid from the Finanzamt carries a one-month Einspruch (objection) window under §355 AO — object in time and the assessment stays open while it is re-examined; let the month lapse and it binds. The notice's own Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung states the clock.

A proposition de rectification from the DGFiP opens its own stated reply window (30 days, extendable on request), and the réclamation through your espace professionnel on impots.gouv.fr is the formal contest route — answer by the letter's date, with your accountant.

Income-tax notices (143(1) mismatches, 139(9) defective returns, 142(1) inquiries) land in the e-filing portal's e-Proceedings and are answered there by the notice's own date — the response flow is electronic end to end against your PAN.

An AT assessment or notice carries its own response window: answer through the portal's e-balcão, and if you disagree the formal route is the reclamação graciosa (120 days) and then judicial review — deadlines bind.

A CRA notice of assessment or reassessment is contested by filing a notice of objection within 90 days of the notice date — respond inside the window or the assessment binds; the CRA's disputes flow is online.

IRAS notices (estimated assessments, queries on the Form C-S/C) are answered through the myTax Portal by the notice's own due date; objections to an assessment follow IRAS's objection process, and the assessed tax stays payable while you object.

ATO review and audit letters set their own response dates; if you disagree with an assessment or decision, the route is a formal objection under Part IVC of the Taxation Administration Act 1953, then review by the Administrative Review Tribunal or appeal to the Federal Court.
NTS notices come with named response tracks (pre-assessment review and the appeal ladder); respond through Hometax or the district tax office named on the notice, inside the window the notice states.

An IRD assessment comes with a hard objection clock: a written objection stating the precise grounds must reach the Commissioner within 1 month after the date of the notice of assessment (Inland Revenue Ordinance section 64), so answer by the date the notice itself states.

Tax Board notices carry their own clocks: a challenge (vaie) against a tax decision goes back to the Tax and Customs Board within 30 days of notification (Taxation Act §§ 137-138), or straight to administrative court; respond through e-MTA or the channel the notice names.
